message.content:
Below are three practical ways to capture a screenshot of a web page that is (or will be) displayed in Google Chrome, all from a Python script.

| Goal | Recommended tool | Why it works |
|------|------------------|--------------|
| **Open a URL in a fresh Chrome instance and grab a screenshot** | `selenium` + `webdriver‑manager` | Selenium drives Chrome like a real browser; `webdriver‑manager` automatically downloads the right ChromeDriver binary. |
| **Attach to an *already running* Chrome window (e.g. the one you’re looking at)** | `pychrome` (Chrome DevTools Protocol) | Chrome can expose a debugging port (`--remote-debugging-port=9222`). `pychrome` talks to that port and can capture the current tab. |
| **Headless, no UI, just a screenshot** | `pyppeteer` (Python port of Puppeteer) | Puppeteer/pyppeteer runs Chrome in headless mode and can capture full‑page screenshots easily. |

Below are step‑by‑step instructions and ready‑to‑run snippets for each approach.

---

## 1️⃣ Selenium – “Open a URL and screenshot”

### Install

```bash
pip install selenium webdriver-manager
```

> **Tip:** `webdriver-manager` automatically downloads the ChromeDriver that matches your installed Chrome version, so you don’t have to manage binaries manually.

### Code

```python
from selenium import webdriver
from webdriver_manager.chrome import ChromeDriverManager
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.service import Service
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options

def screenshot_with_selenium(url: str, output_path: str):
    # Optional: run Chrome headless
    chrome_options = Options()
    chrome_options.add_argument("--headless")          # no UI
    chrome_options.add_argument("--disable-gpu")
    chrome_options.add_argument("--window-size=1920,1080")  # set viewport size

    # Create a Chrome driver instance
    service = Service(ChromeDriverManager().install())
    driver = webdriver.Chrome(service=service, options=chrome_options)

    try:
        driver.get(url)
        # Wait for page to load fully (you can add explicit waits here if needed)
        driver.implicitly_wait(10)

        # Grab screenshot
        driver.save_screenshot(output_path)
        print(f"Screenshot saved to {output_path}")
    finally:
        driver.quit()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    screenshot_with_selenium(
        url="https://www.example.com",
        output_path="example.png"
    )
```

#### Full‑page screenshot

Selenium’s `save_screenshot` only captures the visible viewport. To capture the entire page you can:

```python
# Get page dimensions
total_width = driver.execute_script("return document.body.scrollWidth")
total_height = driver.execute_script("return document.body.scrollHeight")

# Resize window to full page size
driver.set_window_size(total_width, total_height)

# Now screenshot
driver.save_screenshot(output_path)
```

---

## 2️⃣ Attach to an existing Chrome instance (via DevTools)

If you already have Chrome open and want to capture whatever is currently displayed, you can enable remote debugging and connect to it.

### Step 1 – Start Chrome with debugging enabled

Close all Chrome windows, then launch Chrome from the command line:

```bash
# Windows
"C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe" --remote-debugging-port=9222

# macOS
/Applications/Google\ Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google\ Chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222

# Linux
google-chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222
```

> **Note:** If you’re on Windows and Chrome is already running, you can add the flag to the shortcut or use `chrome://flags/#enable-remote-debugging`.

### Step 2 – Install `pychrome`

```bash
pip install pychrome
```

### Step 3 – Python script to capture the active tab

```python
import pychrome

def screenshot_existing_chrome(output_path: str):
    # Connect to the debugging endpoint
    browser = pychrome.Browser(url="http://127.0.0.1:9222")

    # Get list of tabs (targets)
    tabs = browser.list_tab()
    if not tabs:
        raise RuntimeError("No Chrome tabs found. Make sure Chrome is running with --remote-debugging-port.")

    # Pick the first tab (or filter by URL, title, etc.)
    tab = tabs[0]
    tab.start()

    # Enable the Page domain
    tab.call_method("Page.enable")

    # Capture screenshot
    result = tab.call_method("Page.captureScreenshot", format="png")
    with open(output_path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(bytes(result["data"], "utf-8"))
    print(f"Screenshot saved to {output_path}")

    tab.stop()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    screenshot_existing_chrome("current_tab.png")
```

> **Advanced filtering** – If you want to target a specific tab, inspect `tab.url`, `tab.title`, etc., and pick the one that matches your criteria.

---

## 3️⃣ Headless screenshot with `pyppeteer`

`pyppeteer` is a Python port of the Node.js Puppeteer library. It runs Chrome in headless mode and can capture full‑page screenshots with a single line.

### Install

```bash
pip install pyppeteer
```

### Code

```python
import asyncio
from pyppeteer import launch

async def screenshot_pyppeteer(url: str, output_path: str):
    browser = await launch(headless=True, args=['--no-sandbox'])
    page = await browser.newPage()
    await page.goto(url, {'waitUntil': 'networkidle2'})
    await page.screenshot({'path': output_path, 'fullPage': True})
    await browser.close()
    print(f"Screenshot saved to {output_path}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(screenshot_pyppeteer(
        url="https://www.example.com",
        output_path="pyppeteer_example.png"
    ))
```

---

## Quick Checklist

| Task | Tool | Command / Code |
|------|------|----------------|
| Install Selenium + webdriver‑manager | `pip install selenium webdriver-manager` | — |
| Install pychrome | `pip install pychrome` | — |
| Install pyppeteer | `pip install pyppeteer` | — |
| Launch Chrome with debugging port | `chrome.exe --remote-debugging-port=9222` | — |
| Run Selenium script | `python selenium_screenshot.py` | — |
| Run pychrome script | `python pychrome_screenshot.py` | — |
| Run pyppeteer script | `python pyppeteer_screenshot.py` | — |

---

### Which one to choose?

| Scenario | Best tool |
|----------|-----------|
| You just need a quick screenshot of a URL (no existing Chrome) | Selenium (simple, works everywhere) |
| You want to capture whatever is currently open in your *own* Chrome window | pychrome (connects to existing instance) |
| You prefer a headless, lightweight solution without needing ChromeDriver | pyppeteer (runs its own Chromium) |

Feel free to mix and match – e.g., use Selenium for most tasks but fall back to pychrome when you need to capture an already‑open tab. Happy screencapturing!
